executiveSummary: Severe, multi-day flooding across the U.S. Four Corners has caused at least one confirmed death, a second suspected, widespread evacuations, and prolonged access disruptions. View Article Flash flooding and swiftwater rescues were reported in Pagosa Springs (CO), Sedona (AZ), and communities in northern New Mexico, with highways closed and rooftop evacuations conducted. Source Thousands were evacuated in Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Murasu prompted school closures, suspended transport, and heightened flood risk following back-to-back cyclones. View Article In northeast Syria, flash floods killed five people, including four children, and the collapse of a bridge severed a key road between Raqqa and Aleppo. Supporting Report Ecuador remains under a nationwide red alert for heavy rainfall, floods, and landslides; authorities report 14,493 people affected in Esmeraldas and approximately 1.25 million people at risk across multiple coastal provinces. Supporting Report Typhoon Champi caused one death, over 170 injuries, mass flight cancellations, and power outages in Taiwan and nearby Japanese islands. outlook72h: U.S. Southwest: Continued river and drainage responses may sustain access constraints and isolated evacuations where channels remain elevated; debris clearance and safety inspections ongoing. View Article India (Andhra Pradesh): Short-term disruptions to education and transport likely around landfall/peak impact windows; localized flooding possible in low-lying and riverine zones. View Article Ecuador Coastal Provinces: Elevated landslide and surface flooding risk persists under red alert; rural access routes and river crossings remain priority watch points. Supporting Report Confidence: Moderate to High depending on locality and evolving hydrologic conditions.
regionalTrends: Hydrometeorological clustering: Back-to-back storm systems in the U.S. Southwest and consecutive cyclones in the Bay of Bengal elevated cumulative flood risk. Source
Compounded vulnerability: Bridge and roadway failures in Syria and the Southwest U.S. demonstrate critical single points of failure for access and aid delivery. Supporting Report
Urban and camp exposure: Flooding affected downtown areas (e.g., Pagosa Springs) and displacement sites in Syria, increasing shelter, WASH, and protection needs. Source
